candidate.answerReason: Exactly 215 sprinters must be eliminated, and each race eliminates five, requiring 43 races. Full rounds of 36, 6, and 1 races achieve this count, matching choice C.

methods.label: Count eliminated sprinters
methods.explanation:
Count eliminations instead of tracking each sprinter's races, because every race eliminates exactly five people. To leave one champion, exactly \(216-1=215\) sprinters must be eliminated. Each nonchampion is eliminated in exactly one race, so none is omitted or counted twice. The number of races is therefore

\[215\div5=43.\]

This count can be achieved: \(216\div6=36\) first-round races leave \(36\) winners; \(36\div6=6\) second-round races leave \(6\) winners; and one final race determines the champion. Thus \(\boxed{43\text{ races}}\) are needed, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
methods.levelReason: Counts each eliminated entrant once and uses elementary equal-group division, with a concrete schedule establishing feasibility.

candidate.annotationRationale: The route-neutral target is finding a required number of equal-sized groups through a division application, cnm_p084. The written method uses math:double-counting to relate the total eliminated entrants to five eliminations per race. Part-total relationships and the meaning of division provide support. The round schedule verifies that the required count is attainable.
